name: Castel del Monte
description: Castel del Monte stands on a hilltop in Apulia, southeast Italy, near Andria. Emperor Frederick II built it in the 1240s as an eight-sided fortress with an octagonal tower at each corner and an octagonal courtyard at its heart. It has no moat or drawbridge, and its blend of classical, Islamic and Gothic details makes it feel more like a puzzle than a stronghold. You can also find it on Italy's one-cent euro coin.
